Source inventory: Data Models, reviewed for one obligation per unit (RMK-1782). Its one unit, the rule that an id the models hold is a non-empty string, is a single obligation and keeps its id; it carries its level.

Source inventory: Room, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1782). The Room block keeps its id. The RoomStatus table is one unit; the refusal paragraphs are split by sentence, and the MAY that lets a lifecycle record or an identity challenge be refused without a framework event stays with the rule it excepts. The permission to write lifecycle records is may; the record it describes is must where an implementation writes one. The RoomTimers block is a structural unit; the sentence that obliges the timers' transitions, then activity, pause, resume, close, setting and when are split by list item and sentence. An integrator's MAY the implementation honours (reopen, resume, set_room_timers) is must; the stream's single status read around its rows' hooks is may. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: RoomEvent, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1782). The RoomEvent and EventSource blocks, the EventType and EventStatus tables and the reserved metadata.instruction key are single obligations and keep their ids. The EventDirection table stays with the sentence that excludes any other direction; the preservation of raw_payload, the provider field's MUST, SHOULDs and MAY, and the reserved idempotency namespace are split by sentence, the refusal by send_event() and commit_event() conditioned on an implementation offering them. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Event Content, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1782). Each content type's block is one unit and keeps its id. The union's opening paragraph splits into one content per event with every type supported, and the type discriminator. CompositeContent splits into its block, the nesting limit with how levels count, an edit's new content, where a sixth level is refused, and the boundaries that refuse it, one sentence kept whole. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Channel Data, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1782): the MAY that lets a channel type define typed data, with its examples; the SHOULD to define it for each supported type; the MUST to preserve unknown data. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Participant, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1782). The Participant block and the status, identification and verification tables keep their ids. The role table is split from the two sentences on who takes part. Joining and leaving, renaming, resolving, one record per participant and who a sender is are split by sentence and list item; rename_member's SHOULD keeps its level, and what it does once offered is must, conditioned on an implementation offering it. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Identity, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1782): the Identity block as a structural unit, then one unit per sentence on address ownership, resolution scope, link_address, unlink_address, what an unlink leaves, and the form addresses compare in. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: ChannelBinding, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1782). The ChannelBinding block, with the sentence that introduces it, is a structural unit; the addresses table, with its introduction, is one unit, and a declaration's MAY (other keys, or none) is a choice the implementation honours, so must. The correspondent, recipient, chat and group rules are split by sentence; a rationale or an example stays with the rule it explains, and an exception with the rule it excepts. The phone number rules are one unit per list item. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: ChannelCapabilities, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1782). The ChannelCapabilities block keeps its id. Source inventory: Observation, reviewed for one obligation per unit (RMK-1782): the Observation block is a single definition and keeps its id; it carries its level.

Source inventory: Inbound Message, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1782): the InboundMessage block as a structural unit; the room and the channel type a message does not carry; the response scope, kept whole with the integrator's way to scope other work; the voice session's connection; parse_voice_session's SHOULD, and the block of what it returns as a must unit where an implementation offers it. Source inventory: Hook Registration, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1781). The HookRegistration interface block stays whole; each registration rule, room-hook lifetime rule and naming rule is a unit, with its conditions, exceptions and rationale; context a unit needs from its neighbours is in its applies. Where a MAY only grants the integrator a choice the implementation honours (global or per-room hooks), the unit is must. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Hook Triggers, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1781). The paragraph on the Status column, which names the triggers an implementation must fire, is one unit; each sentence on the Execution column and on where a trigger fires is a unit. The trigger table is split one row per unit, with the markers inside its cells so that it renders as before; its header goes with the first row, each group heading with the first row under it. A Planned row is must for an implementation that provides its capability, and untested.json says why no scenario cites it; BEFORE_AI_CONTEXT_BUILD, required by nothing today, is may; the Superseded row is must and untested.json says why. The ON_ERROR payload, the mutation hooks' payload and the lifecycle hooks' context are one unit a sentence, the error categories one a row. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Hook Execution Modes, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1779): a SYNC or ASYNC rule, a rule of who serves a call, an ON_TOOL_CALL rule or a human-input rule per unit, or one sentence of it. Each unit keeps its conditions, exceptions and rationale; context a unit needs from its neighbours is in its applies. What a hook returns binds its author alone and is non_testable (RK-9.3-003). A hook declaring itself fail-closed and a hook replacing a served result or its copy are may (RK-9.3-028, RK-9.3-058); a producer stating an outcome structurally and a delivered human-input outcome staying readable are should (RK-9.3-079, RK-9.3-110). Where a MAY only grants a hook or a model a choice in a sentence that states what the implementation does, the unit is must. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: HookResult, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1781). What a SYNC hook returns binds its author alone and is non_testable (RK-9.4-007), as RK-9.3-003 is; the HookResult interface block that sentence introduces is a unit of its own (RK-9.4-040), and the InjectedEvent block stays with its title (RK-9.4-003). Each rule of a BEFORE_BROADCAST replacement, of injected events and of the triggers that commit them is a unit, with its conditions, exceptions and rationale. Where a MAY only grants a hook a change the implementation honours (RK-9.4-011, RK-9.4-016), the unit is must. Every unit carries its level.
Source inventory: Hook Pipeline (BEFORE_BROADCAST). Its one diagram states one procedure and stays one unit, which carries its level (RMK-1781).

Source inventory: Off-lock checks (`needs_lock = false`), split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1781). The step 5a block stays with the sentence that introduces it (RK-9.5.1-002); each sentence of the Order, Release, Bound, Decision, Errors, Context, Reentrance, the room's work outside the lock, Past the cap, a message routed back and other commit paths rules is a unit, or one list item. Two clauses only an integrator keeps stand alone and are non_testable (RK-9.5.1-016, RK-9.5.1-057). Skipping a streamed row's room read is may (RK-9.5.1-070). Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Turn Execution, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1780): the turn, the room owner's and the turn executor's roles, the default kit's in-memory executor, and the TurnBackend interface, which stays whole as one block (RK-10.6-009). Each unit keeps its conditions, exceptions and rationale. Running executors in any process is may (RK-10.6-008). Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Scope and the one path, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1780): what runs through the backend, what does not, and the one path every backend carries. Each unit keeps its conditions, exceptions and rationale; context a unit needs from its neighbours is in its applies. The in-memory backend handing a request's events as they are is may (RK-10.6.1-014). Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Channels on each side, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1780): the owner's declaration, the executor's factory and what it gives a channel, per-room state and the previous turn, and the state the host sets for the room. The ChannelDeclaration block stays whole (RK-10.6.2-006); each item of what the executor gives a channel is a unit. A bound on the builds an executor keeps and a channel keeping per-room state are may (RK-10.6.2-015, RK-10.6.2-025); what follows once bounded is must. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Messages, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1780). The request block and the tables of frames, control, calls, channel control and messages outside a turn each stay whole as one unit (RK-10.6.3-002, RK-10.6.3-003, RK-10.6.3-004, RK-10.6.3-006, RK-10.6.3-011, RK-10.6.3-034); the prose after each is cut by sentence. Each unit keeps its conditions, exceptions and rationale; context a unit needs from its neighbours is in its applies. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: The stream: pulled, never pushed, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1780): the output, the reader's pace and pull grants, close, what the consumer reads in frames, and when the record is compared. Joining text deltas into one item and checking only for key writes before a delta are may (RK-10.6.4-008, RK-10.6.4-017). Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: What a turn asks of the owner, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1780): owner-served tools, TurnHost, what a turn reads of its room, the turn's record on the owner, the in-memory backend's execution context and human input. The TurnHost block stays with the sentence that introduces it (RK-10.6.5-026). Host-declared verbs are should (RK-10.6.5-028); what they do once offered is must. A host keeping its other kit from an executor's turns binds the host alone and is non_testable (RK-10.6.5-042). Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Hooks, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1780): where a trigger fires, registration, room hooks and the context a hook on the executor receives. The trigger table stays whole (RK-10.6.6-005). Enabling a name already enabled is a no-op that keeps its place, and a name another registration holds is refused (HITL c1206a93; RK-10.6.6-020, RK-10.6.6-021). A host's setup of its turn hooks binds the host alone and is non_testable (RK-10.6.6-011). Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Placement, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1780): what an executor declares, its channel and organization entries, the owner's own executor, one executor per request, the room's state holder, and which agents can answer. Each unit keeps its conditions, exceptions and rationale; context a unit needs from its neighbours is in its applies. A deployment's executor pool binds the deployment alone and is non_testable (RK-10.6.7-008); who may reach the backend's transport shares its sentence with what organizations keep apart and stays behavior (RK-10.6.7-016). Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Liveness, cancellation and errors, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1780): heartbeats and timeouts, cancellation, closing an executor, steering, and error records. Each unit keeps its conditions, exceptions and rationale; context a unit needs from its neighbours is in its applies. A beat outside the turn's numbered messages is may (RK-10.6.8-011). A host declaring its error classes on each side shares its sentence with what each side reads and stays behavior (RK-10.6.8-045). Independent executor closure (RK-10.6.8-028 to RK-10.6.8-034) keeps its evidence partial: remote executors and owned channel factories are not certified by the local scenarios. Every unit carries its level.

Source inventory: Telemetry and prerequisites, split to one obligation per unit (RMK-1780). The same timeouts in every process of a backend and the transport's trust boundary bind the deployment alone and are non_testable (RK-10.6.9-007, RK-10.6.9-010). Every unit carries its level.
